items.passage:
An analytics log records four session segments after the checkout page was replaced.
One: desktop sessions from Canada via search switched on 4 March; by 29 March purchases ran 6 percent above the same segment a month earlier.
Two: desktop sessions from Canada via search switched on 5 March; by 30 March purchases ran 4 percent above the same segment a month earlier.
Prices held steady through each segment's month, matching the earlier period to the nearest cent, and every segment browsed the general catalogue. The counts cover every session, signed in or not, and a quarter of each segment never signed in.
Three: desktop sessions from Canada via search switched on 6 March; by 31 March purchases ran 7 percent above the same segment a month earlier.
Four: desktop sessions from Canada via search switched on 7 March; by 28 March purchases ran 5 percent above the same segment a month earlier.
The log was exported to the reporting spreadsheet each Monday and signed by an analyst.
items.notes: SEED. All four segments share device, country, month and traffic source. The closer neutralises the month-over-month comparison by holding traffic, promotions, prices and other releases fixed.

items.passage:
An analytics log records four session segments after the checkout page was replaced.
One: desktop sessions from Canada via search switched on 4 March; by 29 March purchases ran 6 percent above the same segment a month earlier.
Two: desktop sessions from Canada via search switched on 5 March; by 30 March purchases ran 4 percent above the same segment a month earlier.
A site-wide discount ran through each segment's month, cutting prices by a fifth against the earlier period, and every segment browsed a fixed-price contract catalogue. The counts cover the sessions that signed in, and a quarter of each segment never signed in.
Three: desktop sessions from Canada via search switched on 6 March; by 31 March purchases ran 7 percent above the same segment a month earlier.
Four: desktop sessions from Canada via search switched on 7 March; by 28 March purchases ran 5 percent above the same segment a month earlier.
The log was exported to the reporting spreadsheet each Monday and signed by an analyst.
items.confound_note: The mid-passage line tallies the purchase counts over the sessions that signed in, and the clause beside it records that a quarter of each segment never signed in. The claim is about the new checkout page raising purchases for the segment, so the numbers describe three quarters of the population the claim is about. Signed-in shoppers arrive with saved cards and addresses and convert at different rates from guests, so the uncounted quarter cannot be assumed to have moved with the counted part. All four segments are desktop sessions from Canada via search inside March and each carries the same sign-in gap, so no case in the log supplies what the others leave out.
items.notes: SEED. Cases identical to coherent_true; only the closer differs. The discount works as a single confound precisely because all four segments share the same month.
